topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, themes, and core learning outcomes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Mechanisms of tumorigenesis: genetic alterations, differentiation failure, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cumulative genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt normal cellular differentiation programs and three-dimensional tissue architecture to initiate tumor development.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors: invasion, metastasis, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the histological, pathological, and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant neoplasms, covering local tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, and standardized tumor naming conventions.

topics.label: Pathophysiological impacts, epidemiology, and comparative oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the physiological mechanisms causing cancer morbidity and mortality, alongside tumor incidence patterns across human populations and diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and compare screening strategies and histological markers across different tumor sites.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping details for subsequent practicals and lectures.
